produced_findings.claim: `page()` returns an extra, duplicated item per call `end = offset + page_size + 1` makes `items[offset:end]` return `page_size + 1` elements. For `page(items, 1, 3)`, `items[0:4]` yields 4 items instead of 3; the extra item at index `offset + page_size` also reappears at the start of the next page, since page `N+1`'s own offset is `page_number * page_size == old_offset + page_size`. Every page returns one more item than requested and consecutive pages share a duplicate boundary item, breaking any caller (API pagination, UI list rendering, batch processing) that assumes fixed page sizes and non-overlapping pages.

`format_message(user)` call duplicated across `notify()` branches The new `"sms"` branch (`app/notify.py:6`) repeats the identical `msg = format_message(user)` call already present in the `"email"` branch (`app/notify.py:3`); the formatting step does not vary by `kind`. Message formatting is now expressed twice for a single logical step. A future change to how messages are formatted (or a new channel added the same way) has to be applied in each branch individually, raising the odds that one branch is updated and another is missed.

Command injection via unescaped shell interpolation of `name` The new code builds `cmd = f"tar -czf {name}.tar.gz data/"` and executes it with `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, check=True)`. `name` is interpolated directly into the shell command string with no escaping, quoting, or validation. The prior implementation (`args = ["tar", "-czf", name + ".tar.gz", "data/"]`, run without `shell=True`) passed `name` as a single argv element, which the shell never parsed — that safety property is removed by this change. Any caller that derives `name` from external or user-controlled input (a filename, request parameter, config value, etc.) can achieve arbitrary command execution in the context the archiving process runs in — a classic OS command injection (CWE-78). The function's signature places no constraint on `name`'s character set, so nothing in the contract prevents such a caller from existing now or being added later.
